title: Concentrate Your Forces
summary: Concentrate your energy and resources on a single, intense goal rather than dispersing them. Focusing on quality and intensity brings mastery and stability, whereas scattering your focus introduces uncontrollable variables, leaving you vulnerable to deception and defeat. If expansion is necessary, delegate tasks to a tight, secure circle of trust to minimize risk.
example: The King of Wu aggressively expanded his empire, which scattered his focus, weakened him from the core, and led to his downfall.
The Rothschild banking family maintained power and clarity of decisions by keeping control strictly within their family, avoiding outsiders while expanding across Europe.
reversal: For the weak, dividing forces can act as an insurance policy so that if one fails, another is available.
Clustering together when weak makes you an easy target for a stronger opponent.
Having multiple patrons can provide backup support, though you must avoid becoming like the bat, which belonged to no group and was left with nothing.
The necessity of concentration depends on the nature of your work, your current power level, and your surroundings.
